label: GO after unrewarded a2-rare-S1 trial, scaled by late-episode time (peak trials 70-89)
terms: (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 u") * (ep_dec == 6) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 u") * (ep_dec == 7) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 u") * (ep_dec == 8) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 u") * (ep_dec == 9) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 u") * (ep_trial >= 55) * (tv("action", -2) == 2) * (tv("state", -2) == 1) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 u") * (ep_trial >= 55) * (tv("prev_reward", -1) == 1)
explanation: reset/71 is active only at GO, and almost only when the previous trial was a2 -> S1 (rare) unrewarded (the model-based 'stay on a2' case). Its size depends strongly on how far into the episode the trial is: fitted weights about 0 in trials 50-59, 0.21 in 60-69, 0.58 in 70-79, 0.83 in 80-89 and 0.33 in 90-99. These interactions with episode decile matter: the plain last_is indicator scores only 0.19 beyond timing, a ramp in ep_trial 0.52, and per-decile terms 0.61 (dev). Two small modifiers: it is weaker (-0.16) when the trial before was also a2 -> S1, so repeated a2-rare-S1 trials give a smaller activation, and slightly stronger (+0.09) when that earlier trial was rewarded. Belief / belief_lo, belief_cover, the hidden good state and the upcoming choice add nothing once the pattern x time terms are in. Test R^2 beyond timing 0.638 (dev 0.625), well above the profile's additive 'all' ceiling of 0.26 (the ceiling has no pattern x time interaction). This run uses observed variables only. The earlier explanation using the model's policy / value adds nothing here: the policy-decile table alone gave 0.06, and the observed pattern x time terms are enough.

issues: The core claim holds. On test, the six claimed terms score R^2 beyond timing 0.638, the same as reported. In the profile residuals, GO after 'a2 S1 u' is +0.213 and every other previous-trial pattern is about -0.02. D1 and D2 are exactly 0. Belief_lo and belief_cover interactions inside the pattern add nothing (0.6377 and 0.6378).

The time shape is described wrongly at the end of the episode. 'Peak trials 70-89' and 'decile 9 = 0.33' suggest a decline across trials 90-99, but the drop is steep and inside that decile. Adding a within-decile slope for decile 9 gives weight 0.80 for decile 9 and slope -0.133 per trial, test R^2 0.666. Five per-decile terms plus slopes beat the claimed four-decile terms.

A finer time shape does better than the decile terms. A piecewise-linear ramp (rising from trial ~58, turning down after ~84 and again after ~92) plus two trial-before modifiers reaches test R^2 0.709 (dev 0.703), against 0.638 claimed.

The trial-before modifier is incomplete. When the GO pattern term is split by the trial two back, 'a1 before' (the agent has just switched to a2) gets the most negative weight: -0.26 to -0.29. The repeated 'a2 S1' case gets -0.15 to -0.22, and 'a2 S2' before is the high baseline. The explanation mentions only the repeated a2->S1 suppression.

There is a missed edge case. On each window's first trial the previous trial is unknown (prev_action == -1), so the worst misses are activations of about 1.1 predicted as about 0.09. Adding (phase==GO)*(prev_action==-1)*(prev_reward==0)*late adds about 0.025 on test (0.638 to 0.662). This is a limit of the data window, not a wrong mechanism.
The '+0.09 when the earlier trial was rewarded' modifier is real but small: weight 0.09-0.15, and it adds almost no R^2.
